senses: A caryatid supporting a basket on her head.
A synthetic insecticide, C₂₁H₂₀Cl₂O₃, used to treat head lice, nits, and scabies; as an active ingredient in flea collars; and to eradicate woodworm infestations.
Synonym of cheongsam (“robe worn by Asian men”).
examples: On Tai Street, everyone's wearing masks instead of their traditional Chinese New Year changshan jackets.

senses: The hooded crow.
The hooded gull.
A person afflicted by neuralgia.
A slap or spank. Alternative spellings include patsh, potsh.
The person who performs the circumcision in a Jewish bris.
ety: From Hebrew מוֹהֵל (mohél), but the common pronunciations are borrowed via Yiddish מוהל (moyel).

senses: A very steep cliff.
The brink of a dangerous situation.
ety: First attested in 1598, from Middle French precipice, from Latin praecipitium (“a steep place”), from praeceps (“steep”), from prae + caput (“head”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap- (“head”). Distantly related to precept through Latin praecipiō (“to teach”), from prae + capiō (“take”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap-, *keh₂p- (“to hold; to seize”).

senses: The stomach.
ety: Coined by James Thurber in the 13 Clocks (1950)
examples: Worse. I shall have to rip him from his guggle to his zatch.
He gave some blood to the lab, and five days later was in surgery, “slit,” as he put it, “from gizzard to zatch”

senses: The idea that a given text is a response to what has already been written, be it explicit or implicit.
The reference to another separate and distinct text within a text.
examples: When one studies the intertextuality of "Hamlet", one realises that William Shakespeare must have read thousands of books.
All of these issues—subjectivity, intertextuality, reference, ideology—underlie the problematized relations between history and fiction in postmodernism.

senses: A qanat, in parts of central southern Asia.
A motif in decorative art resembling the fan-shaped leaves of a palm tree.
ety: From French palmette. By surface analysis, palm + -ette.

senses: A tool used to burnish, for making smooth and shiny by rubbing.
A plush stuffed swivel rocking recliner armchair.
ety: Genericized trademark of La-Z-Boy, from lazy + boy.

senses: A deep sleep during which the body is stored at very cold temperature, to preserve it; cryogenic sleep.
Of or related to casuistry, attempting to solve moral dilemmas by application of general rules.
Similar to the arguments of casuists, particularly (figurative, derogatory) overly subtle, hair-splitting.
A hollow between two hills or peaks, especially with a road running through it; a vale.
ety: From Middle English swire, from Old English swēora, from Proto-Germanic *swerhô.

senses: A food preparation common in southern India and Sri Lanka, made of vegetables and lentils (usually pigeon peas, also called toor dal) in a spicy tamarind and lentil flour soup base.
ety: From Tamil சாம்பார் (cāmpār), from Marathi सांभार (sāmbhār)/सांबार (sāmbār, “curry”), from Old Marathi सांबार (sāṃbāra), from Sanskrit सम्भार (sambhārá, “materials required for a particular purpose, provision; collection of spices”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *sambʰārás, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *sambʰārás, from Proto-Indo-European *sem-bʰor-ó-s, from *sem- (“together, one”) + *bʰer- (“to bear, carry”) + *-ós (deverbal suffix). Doublet of Anbar and ambar.

senses: To perform kriging of data.
ety: First used by Georges Matheron, from Danie G. Krige's surname.

senses: Someone who razes.
Having been born out of marriage.
Of no use or purpose; useless; worthless.
A particular Hindu prayer ritual, involving candles made from clarified butter.
ety: Borrowed from Hindi आरती (ārtī), from Sanskrit आरात्रिक (ārātrika).
examples: There is no priest, only an enthusiastic local who leads the aarti by striking a steel plate with a spoon, the lyrics a mash of Hindi and Sanskrit, the lack of melody made up for by gusto.

senses: Sullen or recalcitrant.
To unlock or unbolt a door that had been locked or bolted with a bar.
To remove an impediment that obstructs the passage of (someone or something).
To remove a prohibition.
ety: From Middle English unbarren, equivalent to un- + bar.
examples: Only Enid could dare him at such a time, and even she felt occasionally that sinking of the heart which the bravest of tamers may experience as he unbars the gate of the cage.

senses: The timber of these trees.
examples: Homeowners can also use cedar, at $1.50 to $3 or more per foot, or exotic hardwoods like meranti from Southeast Asia or ipê from Brazil at about $3 a foot.

senses: Synonym of peanut butter cup
ety: A genericization of the trademark Reese, a popular brand of peanut butter cup, thus applied to all peanut butter cups.

senses: To disentangle, remove tangles from (especially hair).
examples: We know that mycorrhizal fungi form and re-form their connections with plants, tangling, detangling and retangling.

senses: The pivoting bar that holds the pickup of a record player and conducts the resulting signal to the amplifier.
A candle holder used in Kwanzaa celebrations.
ety: From Swahili kinara (“candlestick”), ultimately from Arabic مَنَارَة (manāra).

senses: A slow-paced Cuban partner dance in 4:4 time.
Someone who practises bhakti; a person who is devoted to God; a devotee; a worshipper; a religious disciple.
examples: In commenting on these stories, Ganga Giri selects the virtues of suffering and sacrifice exhibited variously by the male bhakts as characteristic of renunciant bhakti.

senses: One who professes a regard for spiritual things only; one whose employment is of a spiritual character; an ecclesiastic.
One who maintains the philosophic doctrine of spiritualism.
One who practises spiritism (a.k.a. spiritualism); a believer in the possibility of communication with the dead; one who attempts to communicate with the dead.
A device that is used to increase the humidity of the air.
examples: Even the plants look expensive. A humidifier hisses beneath her calatheas.

senses: realisation of capital, creation of surplus value, self-expansion of capital, increase in value
ety: From Portuguese valorizacão, from valorizar (“to enhance the value of”; from valor (“value, worth”) + -izar (“-ize”)) + -acão (“-ation”).

senses: To produce a raucous noise like a squawk or honk.
A normal espresso drink, neither ristretto (shorter) nor lungo (longer).
ety: Borrowed from Italian normale (“normal”). Doublet of normal.

senses: A unit of measurement based on one trillion hertz.
One trillion hertz, 10¹² Hz.
A wheel having a groove in the rim for a rope to work in, and set in a block, mast, or similar; the wheel of a pulley.
A sliding scutcheon for covering a keyhole.
ety: From Middle English, from a Germanic base akin to German Scheibe, late Old Norse skífa (“slice”), all ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to split”). For more see shive.

senses: Any material used to seal a surface so as to prevent passage of a fluid.
A mixture of polymers, fillers, and pigments used to fill and seal joints where moderate movement is expected.
Quality or state in which choice or discretion is allowed.
examples: Some offices do not follow the corporate procedure, due to a culture of optionality.
